title: How to share a Canva design link on Mac: step by step, with access levels explained
metaTitle: How to Share a Canva Design Link on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to share a Canva design link on Mac: open Share, set access, pick view, comment or edit, then copy the link. Steps for the desktop app.
targetKeyword: how to share a canva design link on mac
secondaryKeywords: canva can view can comment can edit
intro: To share a Canva design link on Mac, open the design, click Share, and set the access level to Anyone with the link. Then pick Can view, Can comment or Can edit, click Copy link, and paste the link where your recipient will see it.
tldr: Open the design, click Share, and change the access level from Only you to Anyone with the link.
Pick Can view, Can comment or Can edit before you copy the link.
Click Copy link, then paste it with ⌘V into your message or email.
Test the link in a Safari private window (⇧⌘N) before you send it.
Stop access later from Share > Settings > Revoke all access.

blocks.text: A design link lets someone open your Canva design without a file attached. You decide two things: who can open the link, and what they can do once they are in. Most mistakes happen in the second part, so this guide covers permissions as well as clicks.
Before you start with a Canva design link on Mac

This guide covers the Canva desktop app for Mac. Canva's Mac download page says the app works on Macs with Intel and Apple chips, so both kinds of Mac are covered. The page does not list a version number or a minimum macOS version, so the menus on your copy may differ a little.

Check that you own the design or have edit rights. If the design belongs to a colleague or a client, you may not see every share option. Ask the owner to send the link, or ask them to give you the access you need.
Finish the layout first when you can. Share settings are easier to check on a finished file. You can still change access after you send a link, so nothing is locked in once you click Copy link.
Choose the access level before you copy the link

The access level controls who can open the design. Canva starts the share panel on Only you. That keeps the design private until you change it. Leave it there while you are still working on the layout.
Switch to Anyone with the link when you want someone to open the design from the link alone. Anyone who gets the link can open it. Only send it to people you trust.

blocks.caption: Access levels as listed in the share panel.

blocks.text: The permission sits next to the access level. It decides what someone can do after they open the design. Canva offers three permissions: Can view, Can comment and Can edit.

rows: Look at the design, with no changes
Look at the design and leave comments
blocks.caption: Canva permission options from the share panel.

blocks.text: Start with Can view. You can raise the permission later if the person needs more. Giving Can edit by default is a common mistake. It is harder to undo once someone has moved elements or changed text.
Test the link before you send it
A link can look right in your app and still fail for someone else. Test it in a Safari private window before you send it. Press ⇧⌘N, paste the link, and see what opens.

A private window does not share your Canva login, so it gives you a rough view of what a stranger sees. If the design does not open in that window, check the access level again. Then copy the link and test once more.
Read the permission you chose one more time before you send the link. The most common reason for a surprised reply is a permission nobody checked.
Stop sharing a Canva design link
Open Share, click Settings, then choose Revoke all access. The menu path is Share > Settings > Revoke all access. The label says all access, so read the prompt before you confirm.
Narrowing a link is often better than removing everything. Try changing the access level back to Only you first. Then test the link again in a private window to confirm the change took effect.
Fix the common problems with a shared Canva link
Most link problems come from three settings: the access level, the permission and the copy itself. Check those before you assume something is broken.

items: Recipient asks for access: the access level is probably still Only you. Change it to Anyone with the link, then copy the link again.
Recipient can see but cannot change: the permission is Can view or Can comment. Change it to Can edit if the work needs changes.
Share button is missing: your account may not have rights to the design, or an admin may have turned off link sharing. Admins can disable the option.
Link stops working: someone may have used Revoke all access. Open Share, then Settings, and check the current setting before you send a new link.
Menus look different: Canva changes labels over time. Canva's help pages were not available to check this guide, so trust the labels on your screen.

blocks.text: Where Lazur helps on the Share screen

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘, Option and Command together, and ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud, and it looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut.

Ask where the Share button is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask it to walk you through the access level, and it guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it shows the next step. It does not click for you.
This helps when the labels on your copy of Canva do not match this guide. Ask what a menu says, and Lazur reads the screen and explains it. You still make every click.
Lazur does not check the link for you. It cannot tell whether the right people can open it. Test in a private window yourself, as described above.
Link opening settings in your Canva profile

A search result mentions a Link opening setting under your profile, in Settings. It may control how links open on your Mac. Canva's help pages were not available to check this guide, so confirm the steps in Settings yourself.
Common mistakes when sharing a Canva link

items: Copying the link before you set the access level. Set access first, then copy.
Sending Can edit to a client who only needs to approve. Start with Can view.
Forgetting who has the link. Revoke access when the project ends.
Posting the link in a public channel while the design is still a draft. Use direct messages or email instead.
Skipping the private window test. A one-minute check prevents an awkward follow-up email.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes come down to the access level and the permission. Check both every time, and the link usually works on the first try.
Send a PDF when a link is not the right fit

Some people cannot open a link, or the layout matters more than the live file. A PDF is a fixed copy, so the layout stays the same. Use the steps in [How to download Canva design as PDF on Mac](/how-to/download-a-design-as-pdf-in-canva) when you need that instead.
Duplicate a draft before you share it

If the design is still changing, duplicate it first. Share the copy when it is ready. You keep the original for edits and share only the finished version. See [how to duplicate a design in Canva on Mac](/how-to/duplicate-a-design-in-canva).
What to do next

Read the access and permission tables once more before your next share. Then try the steps on a test design. When you are comfortable, look at [Canva for designers on Mac](/for/designers/canva) or [the Lazur guide for Canva](/apps/canva).
If you want Lazur on your Mac, you can [download it here](/download). It starts with a 3-day Pro trial and no credit card, and the trial begins when you first open the app.

faq.question: Can someone open my Canva link without a Canva account?
faq.answer: This guide does not confirm that. Canva's help pages were not available to check, so the account rules for recipients are not covered here. Test the link in a Safari private window to see what a visitor without your login sees.

faq.question: What is the default access level for a Canva design?
faq.answer: The share panel starts on Only you. That setting is the default and keeps the design private. Change it to Anyone with the link only when you are ready for someone else to open the design.

faq.question: Which permission should I choose for a client review?
faq.answer: Start with Can view when you only need approval. Choose Can comment when you want feedback in the design itself. Use Can edit only with people you trust to change the layout.

faq.question: How do I stop someone from opening my design link?
faq.answer: Open Share, click Settings, then choose Revoke all access. Read the prompt before you confirm. You can also change the access level back to Only you, then test again in a private window.

faq.question: Does Lazur click the Share button for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the Share button and guides you one click at a time. You make every click. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask, and Lazur answers out loud. It does not operate Canva for you.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for copying a Canva design link?
faq.answer: This guide does not list one, because Canva's help pages were not available to check. Use the Share menu to copy the link, then paste it with ⌘V.

faq.question: Why does my link open for me but not for others?
faq.answer: Your own login can see the design even when the link does not work for others. Check the access level, then test in a Safari private window. If the window still fails, ask your admin whether link sharing is turned off.

faq.question: Does this guide work for the Canva website too?
faq.answer: No. This guide covers the Mac desktop app. The web version may use different labels, and the differences between the Mac app and the web were not verified here. Check the labels on your screen before you follow the steps.

steps.name: Open the design
steps.text: Open the Canva desktop app on your Mac and open the design you want to share. Check that it is the version the other person should see. Share settings are easier to check on a finished file.

steps.name: Click Share
steps.text: Find the Share button at the top of the editor. Click it to open the share panel.
steps.tip: If you cannot see Share, you may not have rights to the design. Ask the owner to send the link.

steps.name: Open the access level menu
steps.text: In the share panel, find the access level. It starts on Only you, which keeps the design private. Click it to see the other options.
steps.tip: Only you is the safest setting while you are still editing.

steps.name: Choose Anyone with the link
steps.text: Select Anyone with the link. Anyone who has the link can try to open the design, based on the permission you choose next.
steps.tip: Nothing is sent to anyone yet. You still copy and paste the link yourself.

steps.name: Pick a permission
steps.text: Choose Can view, Can comment or Can edit. Pick Can view for a final review, Can comment for feedback, and Can edit only when the person should change the design.
steps.tip: Check the permission before you copy the link. It is the setting people notice first.

steps.name: Copy the link
steps.text: Click Copy link. Canva puts the link on your clipboard. Paste it into your message, email or document before you copy anything else.
steps.tip: Copying a second item replaces the link on your clipboard.

steps.name: Paste and send the link
steps.text: Click where you want the link, then press ⌘V to paste it. Add a line that says which permission you chose, so the person knows whether they can edit or only view.
steps.tip: Say whether they can comment or edit. People often assume they can change the design.

steps.name: Test it in a private window
steps.text: Open the link in a Safari private window to see what a stranger sees. Choose File > New Private Window, or press ⇧⌘N, then paste the link.
steps.tip: A private window does not carry your Canva login, so the test is close to a visitor's view.

troubleshooting.fix: Check that you own the design or have edit rights. If you do not, ask the owner to send the link. On a work or school account, ask your admin whether link sharing is allowed, because admins can turn the option off.

troubleshooting.problem: The person is asked to request access
troubleshooting.fix: The access level is probably still Only you. Open Share, change it to Anyone with the link, copy the link again, and test it in a private window.

troubleshooting.problem: The person can see the design but cannot change it
troubleshooting.fix: The permission is Can view or Can comment. Change it to Can edit if they need to make changes, then send the link again so they have the current version.
Someone may have used Revoke all access. Open Share, then Settings, and check the current setting. Set the access level again and copy a fresh link.
Canva changes its menus over time, and the help pages were not checked for this guide. Trust the label on your screen. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur what it says.

troubleshooting.problem: The private window still shows an error
troubleshooting.fix: Close the window, copy the link again from Share, and try once more. If it still fails, check the access level and ask your admin about link sharing settings.
